pr_comments:
Tested with 251.3 (made sure that rfkill is unblocked **after** networkd tried to configure wlan0). The problem is gone.

Thanks for the prompt reaction!

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
<!-- Make sure to enclose the pasted kernel version in `backticks`, so that
     GitHub doesn't convert the `#` character typically included in it into a
     reference to old GitHub issues. -->
 > `Linux ideapad 5.18.1-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 30 May 2022 17:53:11 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > x86_64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > DHCPv4 address stays regardless of whether networkd has once failed to configure the interface due to rfkill block

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > DHCPv4 address get silently dropped because networkd has once failed to configure the interface due to rfkill block

**Steps to reproduce the problem**

 The network file for my `wlan0` is as simple as:
```
[Match]
Name=wlan0
[Network]
DHCP=ipv4
DNSSEC=no
```
After upgrading systemd from 250.5 to 251.2, I notice that `wlan0` no longer has DHCPv4 address assigned after boot. However when I check log:
```

```
~My hunch told me that it probably has something to do with the code in networkd that deals with IPv6LL, and  it was right: if I add `LinkLocalAddressing=no` to the `.network` for `wlan0`, the DHCPv4 address will not dropped after boot.~

~I can't tell whether the bug is more "racy" in nature or if it really only affects DHCPv4 address, but it doesn't seem to affect the static address assigned on e.g. `bridge0`.~

Actually it seems to *instead* have something to do with the fact that `wlan0` *was once* (note *was once*) "not operable" because it *was* rfkill-blocked. For now I have to disable systemd-networkd and pulls it with my rfkill-unblocking service (which is in turned pulled by `wlan0`):
```
[Unit]
Wants=iwd.service systemd-networkd.service
Before=iwd.service systemd-networkd.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/rfkill unblock wlan

[Install]
WantedBy=sys-subsystem-net-devices-wlan0.device
```

The thing is in my experience `rfkill` itself isn't really "synchronous". Nevertheless, this is obviously a regression in networkd anyway.

P.S. I'm almost 100% certain that it is due to the rfkill block *history*, since the issue does not show up on wired interface or wireless interface on my other laptop that does not have the interface rfkill-blocked on boot.

One should be able to reproduce the problem by having a service run rfkill block on WLAN before networkd is started. (Certainly systemd-rfkill should be masked.)
